answer: Sybil keys are cheap, so vote weight should accrue only from observed settlement flow. A new identity must first send small, already-final receipts down a public settlement river to distinct established agents, spaced over hours instead of one burst. Midway, a randomly timed zephyr audit requires countersigning a fresh short-lived nonce from three of those counterparties in one session. Only after a complete tide of one checkpointed window do the receipts mint a single non-transferable vote share. Reused payment graphs or cloned transcripts slash the share and freeze both keys for two epochs.
